about: Second, independent reading (A2) of the 24 heldout items in heldout_subset_a2.txt, made to measure how often two readers agree. Read only from heldout_stripped.jsonl (sentence, scheme, hypotheses, location), with the checker pinned (HELDOUT_PIN.md) and never run. Same format as dev_readings.json, except: no `actual` or `score` (nothing was run), and since this reader may not add specs, each formalization component names the spec it needs in `spec_needed` (with `spec` null). Reasons follow the taxonomy in README.md; class theorems are not narrowed (README), as in dev (mfa_oslo_notes:20, osher_tadmor_1985_convergence:09).

unformalized.note: Lemma 4.2: every m-stage RK method (4.8) with alpha_ik >= 0 (L~ for negative beta_ik) is TVD with CFL coefficient min alpha_ik/|beta_ik|, for every operator L whose forward Euler step (and L~'s backward step) is TVD; a theorem over all such methods and operators, as dev mfa_oslo_notes:20
Lemma 1.1: every RK method (1.8) with alpha_ik, beta_ik >= 0 is TVD under dt <= min(alpha_ik/beta_ik) dt_1, for every L whose Euler forward step is TVD; a class theorem, as shu1997_icase_notes:03

the CFL coefficient 0.32 is a property of the method's coefficients for every L with a TVD Euler step (as mfa_oslo_notes:20); 'is found' is existential, the three free parameters of the conversion to (1.8) and the z_1..z_6 of (4.2) are not printed in the item, and no claim kind expresses an SSP coefficient or 'two storage units'. Narrowing L to first-order upwind for u_t + a u_x = 0 was considered and rejected: it gives a linear 4-point scheme, but its TVD range would not test the value 0.32 (a coefficient over all L), so the narrowing would not keep the sentence's content

Proposition 3.1: an upper bound c <= 1 on the CFL coefficient over the whole family of m-stage, mth-order SSP RK methods with nonnegative coefficients (L linear); an optimality statement over a class of methods, and no claim kind for an SSP coefficient

Proposition 3.2: the methods (3.1)-(3.2) are mth order and SSP with c = 1 for every linear L with a strongly stable forward Euler step (any norm), i.e. a statement over all L, as mfa_oslo_notes:20, which dev did not narrow. A narrowing to first-order upwind L on u_t + a u_x = 0 for m = 2, 3, 4 (stencil u_{i-4}..u_i), claim tvd_under_cfl with nu_range [0, 1], would be sound in the verify direction, but it would drop the 'mth order' part (the full scheme is first order in dx; no claim kind for the temporal order of an RK method) and is not the precedent. (Checked by hand only that the printed recursion gives the Taylor polynomials for m = 2, 3: 1 + z + z^2/2, 1 + z + z^2/2 + z^3/6.)

Proposition 5.4: optimality (c = 1/3 is the largest) over all four-step third-order methods (2.14) with alpha_i, beta_i >= 0; an optimum over a class, and no claim kind for an SSP coefficient of a multistep method
Proposition 6.2: no implicit RK method of form (6.7) of order >= 2 has all alpha_ik >= 0; a nonexistence theorem over a class of methods
Proposition 6.3: no implicit multistep method of form (6.16) of order >= 2 has all alpha_i >= 0; a nonexistence theorem over a class of methods
a summary of the paper ('we have systematically studied'); the property it names (SSP methods keep forward/backward Euler stability in any norm) is a statement over all SSP methods and operators

the limiter acts on Euler states (density step (2.4)-(2.5), then the pressure step (2.10)-(2.11) through the intersection with the boundary of G_eps, theta_2 over vector states); limiter_accuracy is for the scalar scaling limiter into [m, M]. A density-only component (one-sided bound m = eps) would cover only part of the limiter, and (2.4)-(2.5) are not printed in the item, so it would be written from memory, not the source. 'easy to implement' has no mathematical content
every SSP RK or multistep method applied to the limited Euler scheme keeps the cell averages in G (with the CFL at every stage); a statement over all SSP methods, for the Euler system

Theorem 2.1: for every flux h that is positivity preserving under (1.5) and every degree-k polynomial with point values in G at the Gauss-Lobatto points, the new average is in G under (2.1); G is the Euler admissible set. cell_average_max_principle is the scalar [m, M] analogue; narrowing to a scalar law would change the set G, not only fix free data

positivity of cell-average density and pressure for every DG or FV (ENO, WENO) scheme with a positivity preserving flux plus the limiter and SSP time stepping, 1D and 2D rectangular meshes; alone, 'suitable CFL condition' is also existential
'we prove entropy stability under optimal CFL conditions': no scheme and no CFL bound named; 'optimal' is undefined

entropy stability of every fully discrete scheme (8.1) whose P satisfies (8.8) (scalar) or (8.10) (symmetric systems); the examples (modified Lax-Friedrichs, upwind) illustrate the class. No claim kind expresses a fully discrete cell entropy inequality (entropy_stable_tadmor is semi-discrete), and 'optimal' stays unread

Corollary 4.1: every conservative scheme (4.3) with viscosity Q is entropy stable if Q* <= Q, and only if for three-point schemes; an iff over all Q, as dev tadmor_1987_viscosity:02 (scalar here, so no 'system')
Theorem 5.3: a sufficient condition (5.23) on the viscosity matrix for every scheme (5.22) for systems; the bound C in (5.21) is defined through the entropy-conservative viscosity of the system

readings.reading: the flux (6.3) is entropy conservative (Delta v g* = Delta psi, so the semi-discrete entropy balance holds with zero dissipation and numerical entropy flux v_bar g* - psi_bar) and consistent (g*(u, u) = f(u))
readings.narrowing: N = 1 (a scalar law, as dev fjordholm_mishra_tadmor_2012_tecno:02 narrowed a system statement): r = l = 1, v^1 = v_nu, v^2 = v_{nu+1}, so (6.3) is g* = (psi(v_{nu+1}) - psi(v_nu))/(v_{nu+1} - v_nu), the scalar (4.4); Burgers' f = u^2/2 with U = u^2/2, F = u^3/3, v = u, psi = v f - F = u^3/6, so g* = (uL^2 + uL uR + uR^2)/6 after cancelling uR - uL (the spec would hold this polynomial; the cancellation is the only algebra done by the reader). 'Consistent with (2.5)' read as consistency of the numerical flux with f; (2.5) is not printed in the item

formalization.spec_needed: scalar Burgers, numerical flux (uL^2 + uL uR + uR^2)/6, eta = u^2/2, entropy_flux = v_bar F - psi_bar with v_bar = (uL + uR)/2, psi = u^3/6, dissipation 0 (as tecno-entropy-conservative-burgers.json)
formalization.bridge: 'entropy-conservative' read as the semi-discrete entropy balance with zero dissipation

unformalized.note: 'second-order accurate' for a semi-discrete scheme has no claim kind (as dev tadmor_1987_viscosity:01; a scalar N = 1 narrowing would be allowed, so 'system' does not block). The entropy-stable conjunct alone cannot be written either: scheme (6.10) itself is not printed in the item (only its viscosity amplitude (6.12), an integral along the path)

readings.reading: the scheme (6.14) is second-order accurate AND entropy stable in the semi-discrete sense for U = u^2/2
readings.narrowing: N = 1 (scalar, as tadmor_2003_acta:12): r = l = 1, u^1_{nu+1/2} = u_nu, u^2_{nu+1/2} = u_{nu+1}, a_1 = f'; Burgers' f = u^2/2, a(u) = u, entropy pair U = u^2/2, F = u^3/3. The scheme is read as printed: numerical flux g_{nu+1/2} = (f(u_nu) + f(u_{nu+1}))/2 - (1/8)[a(u_{nu+1}) - a(u_nu)]^+, with [x]^+ = max(x, 0); the printed (6.14) has no <l^j, Delta v> factor on the viscosity term, which the printed bound (6.13) has, and the reading does not add it. The path hypothesis is void for N = 1

formalization.unformalized: second-order accurate: no named claim for semi-discrete order of accuracy (as dev tecno:02)

formalization.spec_needed: scalar Burgers, semi-discrete, numerical flux (uL^2/2 + uR^2/2)/2 - max(uR - uL, 0)/8, entropy u^2/2 with flux u^3/3

unformalized.note: Corollary 8.2: a fully discrete cell entropy inequality for every scheme (8.1) for a symmetric system whose P satisfies (8.10); no claim kind for a fully discrete cell entropy inequality

readings.reading: WENO5M (mapped weights (43)-(46)) is fifth order where f' != 0 and also at a critical point with f' = 0, f'' != 0, eps = 0
readings.narrowing: 'optimal order' read as 2r - 1 = 5 for r = 3; 'near critical points' read as at a first-order critical point (n_cp = 1, the item's hypothesis), plus the generic regime for 'even'; one split flux component, the order as the truncation error of (f^_{j+1/2} - f^_{j-1/2})/dx at one grid point ('convergence' read through the local truncation error, as dev jiang_shu_1995_weno:01); eps = 0 as the hypothesis states

formalization.spec_needed: WENO5 with Jiang-Shu indicators and the mapping g_k of (43) applied to the Jiang-Shu weights, renormalized (46); candidate fluxes (15)

unformalized.note: the bare sentence fixes neither eps nor its scaling with dx, nor the order of the critical point (the hypotheses say the mapping is ineffective for n_cp = r - 1 = 2); its truth depends on that choice, as dev jiang_shu_1995_weno:01 alone
'similarly afflicted' is vague (which order is lost, at which n_cp), and the higher-order schemes are not defined in this source (only cited), so no spec can be written from the item

readings.reading: WENO5M is fifth order on smooth solutions (f' != 0, and at first-order critical points), eps = 0, AND its accuracy gain over WENO5 is more modest for flows with discontinuities
readings.narrowing: as henrick_aslam_powers_2005_mapped:05: r = 3, flux difference at one grid point, eps = 0, critical points of order n_cp = 1 (the hypothesis)

formalization.unformalized: 'the improvement in accuracy is more modest when flows with embedded discontinuities are considered': a numerical comparison (Sod problem, Table 9), not-checkable

unformalized.note: alone, eps and the order of critical points of the smooth solutions are open (as :05 alone), and the second clause is a numerical comparison
an observed convergence rate (no more than first order in L1) on Euler test problems with discontinuities, with RK3 time stepping
